headline: NQ holds in the CME weekend halt with no live price path: Tail stays at the 2% floor and EA_ON, while Stress lifts to 12% on unresolved Hormuz headline risk carrying into Sunday's reopen.
body: NQ futures remain inside the CME weekend halt that began at Friday's 21:00 UTC weekly close, so for the third consecutive run there is no live price path to evaluate for directional efficiency, shallow pullbacks or repeated extension. The assessment therefore rests on the last confirmed cash session plus corroborated news, and that limitation is the main driver of the low Confidence reading rather than any judgement about market calm. Last confirmed structure: Friday's U.S. cash session closed constructively, with the Nasdaq Composite up roughly 0.8% at about 26,803 and the S&P 500 up about 0.7% near 7,800 after the week's softer inflation prints, and the Russell 2000 setting a fresh record to cap the week. VIX's last confirmed print is about 14.63, a calm level entirely inconsistent with a stressed or one-way tape, and WTI's last confirmed level is near $81 with no Friday risk premium expansion. None of this is a currently observable price path; it is the most recent verified state carried into the halt. Geopolitics is the one live channel this hour. The Strait of Hormuz crisis remains unresolved: the UAE has attributed Thursday evening's drone attack on two ADNOC vessels to Iran, ADNOC reports 15 of its vessels struck since the conflict began including three this week, and Qatar, Kuwait, Egypt and Bahrain have issued condemnations. WebSearch this hour surfaced only recap and live-blog coverage of that same episode, so no new discrete escalation is confirmed since the prior run. What has changed is timing rather than facts: the market is now fully inside the weekend window, and this crisis has already produced a weekend incident once (the prior ADNOC tanker attack was reported Saturday 8 August). That precedent is a concrete reason not to let Stress decay to a trivial floor, and Stress is accordingly raised to 12% from the prior run's 9%. Calendar work this hour: the FOMC minutes from the 28-29 July meeting are confirmed for Wednesday 19 August at 18:00 UTC, the single high-impact item in the next seven days but well outside this 24-hour horizon. The Jackson Hole symposium was checked and falls on 27-29 August, outside the seven-day window, so it is excluded from the event list rather than carried as an imminent catalyst. Housing starts and building permits appear in week-ahead previews with conflicting dates and are omitted rather than guessed. Data availability: the Alpha Vantage free-tier daily quota is again exhausted (MARKET_STATUS returned a rate_limit error), so this run used no Alpha Vantage figures and relies entirely on WebSearch corroboration. Confidence is 37% (low), a point above the prior run because the next-week calendar and Friday's closing levels were independently re-verified this hour, but still low because no live price structure is obtainable. Assessment: Tail is 2% (low) and the action stays EA_ON with a green status, derived from current Tail alone. Stress is 12% (low) reflecting the weekend halt floor plus a standing Middle East headline premium. The danger window is anchored to the CME Sunday reopen at roughly 22:00-23:00 UTC on 16 August, which is where any accumulated weekend headline risk would express itself as a gap; it is not a generic window around this run. Existing-position management, exits and emergency protection remain active regardless of the EA_ON state. This is general market-risk assessment, not personalised financial advice.

lookbackSummary: Over the trailing 24 hours Tail never left the low band, running 13% at Thursday's 23:00 UTC slot and grinding down through the Asian and European sessions to 9% as Thursday's CPI/PPI digestion faded without producing one-way structure. Stress described a clear event arc: it eased to 23% in the quiet pre-dawn hours, rebuilt to 33-44% across the U.S. cash session as Friday's Retail Sales and UMich prints and a semiconductor drag created two-way volatility without directional efficiency, and then collapsed to 12% once the 21:00 UTC CME weekly close removed the tape entirely. Tail actually fell into the close (9% at 19:00, 6% at 21:00, 2% at 22:00), consistent with a session that ended constructively rather than in forced one-way repricing. Confidence peaked at 58% around the 13:00 UTC data window when live prints were verifiable and decayed to 37% by the final hour as Alpha Vantage's daily quota ran out and the halt removed live price evidence. One slot, 20:00 UTC, has no published Claude assessment and is marked unavailable rather than backfilled.
outlookSummary: The entire 24-hour horizon sits inside the CME weekend halt: it ends at 22:00 UTC Saturday, roughly a full day before the Sunday reopen near 22:00-23:00 UTC. Tail is therefore projected to hold at the 2% floor through Saturday morning and to tick only marginally to 3% in the later slots, reflecting the approach of the reopen rather than any observed structure - a pathological price path cannot form while no venue is quoting. Stress is projected to hold near 10-13% across the window, easing slightly through the quiet Saturday hours and firming into the final slots as the Sunday gap comes into view with the Hormuz crisis unresolved. Confidence decays steadily from 37% toward 29% because the evidence set cannot be refreshed with live price data and Alpha Vantage's quota does not reset within the window. Every forecast slot maps to EA_ON and green. The first genuine re-scoring opportunity is the reopen, where an escalation-driven gap would be scored on observed price path rather than anticipated.
